questions.note: Order right: hallux longest, toe 2 ends ~10 mm short (as built), 1-2 gap ~5 mm under the pulps. Shaping weak: toe 2 an even cylinder with no PIP knuckle, both pulps boxy from below, toe 2's plantar PIP crease a sharp ledge, wrinkles identical carved rings, distal hallux a thin wedge (~15.6 mm deep at the nail root vs 19; medial view, 17.9 px/mm).

Hallux and toe 2 only (3-5 declared). Good: free-edge thickness visible (~1 mm), trimmed straight, pink bed through the plate, widths ~20.5 and ~10.5 mm (front view, 21.7 px/mm). Wrong: flat tiles with no dome, an exposed white proximal lip with no cuticle or crescent lunula, torn sawtooth hallux corners, a box-cut slot under toe 2's edge, heavy striations.

Extensor relief is real relief that catches the light, not drawn, but it stops short: the EHL ridge fades before the first MTP and doesn't cross it, no slip shows toward toe 2, and the dorsum in frame has no dorsal or digital veins. The saphenous is outside these frames and not judged.

SSS believable: shadow sides stay dark, no glow, tips slightly redder. Micro-relief present but wrong in kind: a uniform outlined-polygon crackle at 0.4-0.9 mm (spec 0.25-0.4) on every surface, no follicle pits, pad ridges straight parallel stripes with no whorls that cross the creases; pads read rubbery. Colour and sheen not counted (first-pass materials).

defects.what: Both distal corners of the hallux nail end in jagged grey sawtooth shreds of torn geometry: the medial one boxed here, the lateral at about [1708, 983, 2000, 1314]. Both also show at native size in pair_hr.hallux_eval and at the tip in medial_eval.
defects.fix: Run the lateral folds and the hyponychium smoothly into the free edge's corners with no spiky displacement. A real corner shows only a soft groove and at most a faint dark grime line under the edge.

defects.what: A strip of torn, spiky geometry runs down the 1-2 web cleft where the hallux's lateral side meets the web. In pair_hr.toe2_eval it renders as a black jagged crack (about [197, 98, 248, 362]); it also shows in front_form and top34_form.
defects.fix: The web is one continuous fold of skin from the hallux's lateral side to toe 2's medial side. Remove the self-intersection or tear so the cleft shades as a smooth, soft crease.

defects.what: The distal hallux is too thin and tapers to a pointed wedge. At 17.9 px/mm the silhouette is ~280 px (~15.6 mm) deep at the nail root against 19 mm, outside +/-2, and ~21 mm at the IP against 22 (~25 after the broadening).
defects.fix: Keep about 19-20 mm of depth to the nail root, and give the distal phalanx a full rounded pulp that bulges below and just beyond the free edge so the tip ends blunt, not pointed.

defects.what: The hallux plate's proximal end is a thick, glossy white lip lying on the skin: no eponychium or cuticle overlaps it, and the pale band is a straight bevelled strip rather than a crescent lunula. It reads as a glued-on press-on nail.
defects.fix: Tuck the root under a proximal fold 1.5 mm wide with a 0.4 mm eponychium and a thin cuticle on the plate, with a matte 3.5 mm half-moon lunula, convex distally, emerging from under it.

defects.what: The hallux plate is a flat rounded square in a rectangular pocket, its matcap shading uniform edge to edge, and toe 2's plate is the same. Neither has the transverse dome of its 11 mm or 6 mm radius.
defects.fix: Dome each plate side to side to its radius (about 6 mm of sag across the 19.5 mm hallux nail) and let its lateral edges sink under soft lateral folds into the nail grooves rather than standing on a ledge.

defects.what: From below both pulps are boxy. Toe 2's is a rectangle with parallel sides and a squared, nearly square-cornered end; the hallux pad is a rounded brick with straight sides.
defects.fix: Make the pulps oval, bulbous pads, widest over the distal phalanx tuft and narrowing to a rounded arc at the tip, with the soft tissue bulging slightly beyond the bone at the sides.

defects.what: The friction ridges are straight parallel stripes at one fixed angle across the sole, the hallux pad and toe 2's pad, running straight through the IP flexion crease. No whorl, loop or arch, and no ridge endings or forks.
defects.fix: Give each toe pad its own whorl, loop or arch centred on the pulp at 0.45 mm pitch, the ridges curving round the tip, broken by forks and endings, and interrupted at every flexion crease.

defects.what: The hallux IP wrinkles are three identical, evenly spaced, smoothly carved ring grooves. Toe 2's PIP has the same set (about [1056, 279, 1501, 528]) and its DIP a single clean cut: machined and copy-pasted.
defects.fix: Use 3-6 irregular creases per joint, varying in length, depth (~0.2 mm) and spacing, some forking or merging and fading out at the sides, with each joint's set different from the others.

defects.what: Toe 2's plantar PIP crease is a straight, sharp-edged ledge across the full width of the toe: the distal segment steps up like the cuff of a sleeve instead of the skin folding.
defects.fix: A flexed PIP folds the plantar skin into a soft, slightly curved crease (~0.5 mm deep) with rounded lips and a little bunching, fading toward the sides.

defects.what: Under toe 2's free edge the distal groove is a flat-floored rectangular slot with vertical walls at both ends, as if box-cut into the tip, and the free edge has a small V drip at its centre.
defects.fix: Shape the hyponychium as a shallow, rounded groove where the tip skin meets the underside of the plate, with about 1.2 mm of free edge overhanging it and no straight walls or square corners.

defects.what: The toe skin is a uniform crackle of dark-outlined polygons about 40-90 px (0.4-0.9 mm at 98 px/mm) against the spec's 0.25-0.4 mm, equally deep everywhere and continuing over the tip: crazed porcelain or lizard skin.
defects.fix: Use finer cells (0.25-0.4 mm) with directional primary lines along the tension lines and fainter secondaries, as low relief rather than dark outlines, and blend into ridged skin round the tip.

defects.what: A single thin, raised, glossy line arcs across the dorsum of the first MTP joint and reads as a healed bunionectomy incision scar. It also shows in top34_eval at about [414, 507, 693, 652].
defects.fix: Over the first MTP dorsum a real foot shows a few short, soft, irregular transverse creases or none, with the EHL tendon's ridge crossing the joint.

defects.what: Toe 2's plate is combed with strong white, high-contrast longitudinal streaks like brushed acrylic, and the hallux plate shows the same in its highlight. At 0.01 mm deep these ridges should barely read.
defects.fix: Keep the ridging at 0.25 mm pitch and about 0.01 mm deep, so it shows only as a faint ripple in a raking highlight, never as white stripes.

defects.what: Toe 2 is a smooth cylinder of nearly even width from the PIP to the tip, with no dorsal knuckle at the head of the proximal phalanx and no waist over the middle phalanx. A sausage toe (spec 8.4) that reads as a finger.
defects.fix: Raise a PIP knuckle (the condyles of the phalanx head under slightly thicker skin), narrow the middle phalanx and let the distal pulp bulge, so the curled toe reads jointed.

defects.what: The EHL relief fades out before the first MTP and doesn't cross the joint, no extensor slip shows toward toe 2, and the forefoot dorsum in frame has no dorsal metatarsal or digital veins at all.
defects.fix: In a lean man the EHL stands as a 1-1.5 mm cord over the first MTP to the hallux base, and dorsal veins about 0.7 mm proud run between the MT heads toward the web spaces.

defects.what: No plantar crease at the hallux's base: the ball runs smoothly into the toe's proximal pad with no sulcus where the spec's ball crease starts at (-48, -200), while toe 2 has its base crease at the web line.
defects.fix: Cut the curved ball crease (1.5 mm wide, 0.8 mm deep) across the hallux base under the MT1 head, so the toe's proximal pad reads separate from the ball, as on a real sole.

ranked: [D4] The nails read as press-on tiles: the hallux plate's proximal end is a thick, glossy white lip lying on the skin, with no eponychium or cuticle over it and no crescent lunula. A real proximal fold overlaps the root and the lunula shows as a matte half-moon.

[D5] Both plates are flat rounded squares set in rectangular pockets. A hallux nail with an 11 mm transverse radius (6 mm on toe 2) is clearly domed side to side, its lateral edges diving into the nail grooves under soft folds.

[D3] In medial profile the distal hallux is a thin wedge tapering to a point at the nail (~15.6 mm deep at the nail root against 19). A real hallux ends blunt, with a full rounded pulp bulging below and just beyond the free edge.
[D6] From below the pulps are blocks: toe 2 is a rectangle with parallel sides and a squared end, the hallux a rounded brick. Real pulps are oval, bulbous pads that narrow to a rounded tip.

[D1] Both distal corners of the hallux nail end in jagged grey sawtooth shreds, plain to see in the closeup at native size. Nothing in a real nail corner looks torn: the folds run smooth into the free edge.
[D2] A strip of torn, spiky geometry in the 1-2 web cleft renders as a black jagged crack beside the hallux. The web is one continuous, smooth fold of skin.

[D7] The plantar friction ridges are straight parallel stripes at one angle over the sole and both pads, running straight over the flexion creases like corduroy. Real pads carry a whorl, loop or arch each, with forks and endings, and the ridges stop at the creases.
[D14] Toe 2 is a smooth, even cylinder with no PIP knuckle or waist over the middle phalanx. It reads as a finger or sausage rather than a curled second toe with a bony knuckle.

[D8] Knuckle wrinkles are 3-4 identical, evenly spaced, smoothly carved rings, the same on the hallux IP and toe 2 PIP, and toe 2's DIP is one clean cut. Real creases are irregular, uneven in depth and length, fork, and fade out at the sides.

The toes read young and clean, close to a mannequin's: the hallux is puffy and evenly rounded with no bony IP condyles, and both proximal phalanges are hairless (hair itself is outside this round's questions).
[D16] From below the hallux grows straight out of the ball with no base crease. A real sole shows a deep curved fold where the toe's pad meets the ball under the first metatarsal head.
[D9] Under toe 2 the PIP flexion crease is a straight, sharp-edged ledge across the whole toe, the distal part stepping up like a sleeve cuff, where real skin forms a soft fold.
[D10] Beneath toe 2's free edge the distal groove is a box-cut rectangular slot with vertical walls and a flat floor. The real hyponychium is a shallow, rounded groove.

[D11] The toe skin is a uniform crackle of dark-outlined polygons about twice the spec's size (0.4-0.9 against 0.25-0.4 mm), equally deep everywhere and continuing over the tip: crazed porcelain or lizard skin rather than human skin lines.

The free edges are perfectly smooth, glossy, opaque white bands with rounded bevels, like a French manicure. A trimmed toenail's edge is ivory, matte, a little irregular, with a faint grime line beneath.
[D12] A thin, raised, glossy line arcs across the first MTP dorsum. A podiatrist would read it as a healed bunionectomy incision rather than a skin crease.
[D13] The nail plates are combed with strong white longitudinal streaks like brushed acrylic. A 40-year-old's ridging is faint and shows only in a raking highlight.

[D15] The tendons stop short: the EHL ridge fades before the first MTP, no extensor slip shows toward toe 2, and the forefoot dorsum in frame has no veins at all, where a lean soldier's foot shows dorsal metatarsal veins.
A small round bead like a blister sits on the hallux's proximal nail fold, best seen in the clay views (front_form, top34_form, hallux_form).
